qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Leading global consumer healthcare portfolio (Sensodyne, Advil, Voltaren, Panadol, Centrum) with high professional dental and pharmacy endorsement. However, the business is burdened by £25.6B in goodwill/intangibles and £7.7B in net debt created by the GSK/Pfizer JV carve-out. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is only 6.6% (2022: 5.1%, 2023: 5.6%, 2024: 7.6%, 2025: 8.6%), failing the 12% hurdle, while OTC categories face persistent private-label substitution pressure.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3b = N, REJECT). World #1 consumer healthcare player with leading OTC brands, but permanent capital structure created by GSK/Pfizer carve-out carries £25.6B goodwill/intangibles resulting in sub-hurdle 6.6% 5-year median GAAP ROIC (FY25 8.6%). Persistent private-label substitution caps pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: GAAP ROIC spans 5.1% to 8.6% across 2022-2025 (median 6.59%), missing the 12% standard. Total debt is £7.66B against £1.26B cash. Despite strong FCF conversion (£2.19B FCF in 2025) and professional brand loyalty for Sensodyne, low return on total capital employed and retail private-label pricing ceiling prevent a Quality Pass.
